newsitem.title: IRAN: Sudanese vice-president in Iran for talks on war.
newsitem.headline: Sudanese vice-president in Iran for talks on war.

text.p: Sudanese Vice-President al-Zubeir Mohammad Saleh arrived in Tehran on Tuesday for talks on the conflict in Sudan, state-run Tehran radio said.

"While a great conspiracy threatens to disrupt Sudan's national unity, the government of our country deems it necessary to consult with our friends in the region and the Islamic world, especially the Islamic Republic of Iran," Saleh told Iran's First Vice-President Hassan Habibi, the radio reported.
Habibi said the two countries would exchange views on the conflict in Sudan and discuss bilateral ties.
Tehran has close ties with Khartoum's Islamist government. Iran has condemned "all acts of aggression" in Sudan and has supported the country's unity and territorial integrity.

Iranian media have accused the United States and Israel of conspiring to bring down the Khartoum government. Washington accuses both Tehran and Khartoum of sponsoring terrorism, which the two countries deny.
Sudan has denied rebel reports Iran has given the Sudanese army weapons, including banned chemical arms, cash and even troops for the fighting.
Sudan says Ethiopia and Eritrea are behind the clashes in the east of the country. Both neighbouring states and the rebels deny this.
Iran, which last year mediated in Sudan's conflict with Uganda, has called on the Organisation of the Islamic Conference and the Arab League to help end the crisis.
Saleh earlier this month explained Khartoum's view of the conflict in Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Syria.
